title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-03-11.json
content:
Perf benchmarking sync notes — 2026-03-11

Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Santos, Riley Chen, Samir Gupta, Taylor Nguyen, + SRE (joined late)

Agenda:
- Quick recap of regression signals from 03/08–03/10 runs
- Repro results and narrowed hypotheses (kernel selection change v2)
- Action items: short-term mitigations and tests to run before next release
- Rollout/fallback plan and observability gaps

Summary / TL;DR:
- We observed consistent latency and throughput regressions after merging kernel-selection heuristics PR (see linked PR).
- p95 increased ~45–55% on long-seq workloads (seq_len 1024) on A100; p50 increased ~30–35%. Throughput (tokens/sec) dropped ~20–25% for batch size 8. Short-seq (128) workloads show smaller regressions (~5–10%).
- Root cause likely related to a suboptimal matmul kernel chosen for certain attention shapes and quantized models (q4 variants). Also saw a KV-cache invalidation micro-regression in the new prefetch path that increases memcpy stalls for multi-request workloads.

Repro notes (how we ran tests):
- Harness: infra/perf/harness/run_bench.py (internal); use --profile-op-level --repeat 10 --seed 42
- Command used (example): python run_bench.py --model redwood-v2-13B-q4 --device a100:0 --seq-len 1024 --batch 8 --profile-op-level --outdir /tmp/perf-runs/2026-03-11
- Bench VM: perf-a100-6 (CUDA 12.2 / cuBLAS 12.2), runtime built from commit 1f3b9a (kernel-selection change merged)
- Observed numbers (median across 10 runs):
  - baseline (pre-change, commit 1d9a7c): p50=118ms, p95=245ms, tokens/sec=420
  - after change (commit 1f3b9a): p50=159ms (+35%), p95=368ms (+50%), tokens/sec=318 (-24%)
- H100 runs show similar direction but smaller magnitude: p95 +30%, tokens/sec -15%

What profiling shows:
- Op-level trace points to attention matmul having lower GPU utilization (occupancy) when kernel-selection picks algorithm A over B for shapes where B is better.
- Additional hotspot: increased memcpy from KV cache prefetch path — microbenchmark shows extra 0.8–1.5ms per request under bursty load due to memcpy+sync semantics introduced in prefetch patch.
- GPU timelines: longer idle gaps between kernels when processing long sequences — suggests kernel launch ordering or streams interactions changed.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selection heuristic mismatch: heuristics pick a kernel optimized for different strides; on some seq lengths this results in worse effective throughput (most likely).
2) Prefetch path introduced sync points (memcpy + cudaStreamSynchronize) that reduce overlap between memcpy and compute under multi-request scenarios.
3) Quantized kernel performance regressions: q4 kernels rely on specific tiling; small off-by-one in shape rounding leads to non-vectorized path.

Quick experiments run today:
- Re-ran with kernel-selection pinned to previous heuristic (env var RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy) -> numbers returned to baseline (within 5%). Good signal that kernel selection is main driver. (Riley)
- Disabled prefetch path -> small improvement (~3–5% p95) but not full recovery. (Samir)
- Ran microkernel throughput benchmarks across shapes -> confirmed that for (seq=1024, head=64, dim=64) kernel B > kernel A by ~1.4x on A100. (Miguel)

Immediate actions (owners + ETA):
- Roll a hotfix to pin kernel-selection to legacy heuristic for the next staging rollout. Owner: Riley; ETA: 2026-03-12 EOD. Status: in progress.
- Add unit/integration tests to perf CI to cover the specific attention shapes (seq 512/1024, batch 4/8) so future heuristics changes are caught. Owner: Taylor; ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Instrument kernel-selection decision logs (add telemetry that records chosen algorithm + input shapes) and surface in perf dashboard. Owner: Miguel; ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Investigate prefetch path to remove syncs / convert to async memcpy using CUDA kernels or pinned buffers. Owner: Samir; ETA: 2026-03-19.
- Open JIRA tickets for (a) kernel-selection bug, (b) prefetch sync issue, (c) perf CI gaps. See linked_artifacts for keys. Owner: Asha; ETA: 2026-03-11 (today).

Rollout/fallback plan:
- Short-term: Pin to legacy kernel-selection in staging and canary for 24–48h. If metrics stable, schedule rollback of the heuristics change from main branch.
- Medium-term: Rework heuristics to consult microkernel benchmarks at build-time and include a safety check in runtime that re-evaluates kernel choice on first N inferences per new shape.

Observability gaps:
- We currently lack a lightweight telemetry field that ties latency spikes to the chosen low-level kernel. Adding this will make root-cause detection faster.
- Perf CI does not cover long-seq/batch combos often used by customers (we must add these).

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Is the kernel-selection change beneficial on other hardware shapes (e.g., H100 or multi-GPU MCM workloads)? Need systematic matrix runs.
- Should we include a remote fallback that, on first N requests, runs a short AB test between two kernels and picks the winner? Operational cost unclear.

Notes to self / informal: 
- Remember: before reverting, check if any other PRs depend on the new kernel API change (breaking changes). Merge graph shows PR #2501 touches same files.
- Slack thread: #perf-alerts has raw traces and a few customer-reported timeouts (partial). Put a short summary there once pinned mitigation is in place.

Next sync: 2026-03-13 10:00 PT (short standup after hotfix rollout)

Action item summary (by owner):
- Asha: file JIRA tickets, customer comms draft, coordinate canary (ETA 03/11)
- Riley: pin kernel-selection hotfix + staging canary (ETA 03/12)
- Miguel: implement kernel-selection telemetry + microkernel bench matrix (ETA 03/16)
- Samir: audit prefetch path for syncs, run async memcpy experiment (ETA 03/19)
- Taylor: add perf CI cases for long-seq/batch combos (ETA 03/18)

Appendix (quick links):
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2486
- Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/benchmarks/serving-runtime-latency?from=2026-03-08&to=2026-03-11
- Repro command example (again): python run_bench.py --model redwood-v2-13B-q4 --device a100:0 --seq-len 1024 --batch 8 --profile-op-level

-- end of notes
